children: A Workspace is Barkpark's top tenancy boundary — every Document, edge, and search index lives under exactly one, and a nil Workspace fails closed.
Workspace is the widest tenant scope in Barkpark, paired with Project as the inner ring. In production two tenants exist: the
(5638273c…) with project ae13a01b…. Every Dataset, and therefore every Document in it, is owned by one Workspace.
Tenancy here is a hard security boundary, not a soft filter. Both
fail closed on a nil Workspace

: if the Workspace cannot be resolved, the Edge Projector refuses to project edges and Postgres Search returns nothing rather than risk leaking another tenant's content into the Content Graph or a result set. Cross-tenant bleed is treated as a correctness bug, so the absence of a Workspace yields emptiness, never a guess.

The Workspace scope threads through every mutation, every Webhooks dispatch, and every Blue Green Rebuild. The Content Graph corpus, Search Facets, and Graph Traversal are all computed within a single Workspace — you never see edges spanning tenants. The active Workspace is part of Auth and Tokens resolution on the HTTP API v1, and the Capabilities Manifest is itself tier-keyed within the Workspace context. The active Perspective (published vs drafts) and the block content of a PortableDoc are both read within this same Workspace scope — nothing is visible outside the tenant that owns it.
